newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Dec 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Dec 3.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Dec. 3:

WASHINGTON - The atmosphere of goodwill that has prevailed between the White House and Congress since last month's election is coming under increasing strain as each day brings new revelations in the Democratic fundraising imbroglio followed by fresh promises of Republican-led hearings.

WASHINGTON - After months of discussion, television industry executives have tentatively agreed to a rating system that will categorize TV programs based on their appropriateness for children of various ages.

WASHINGTON - President Clinton faces a choice as he returns this week to the business of staffing his administration: He will either make history by appointing a woman in one of the top spots on his national security team or risk disappointing many of the very voters who produced his margin of victory in last month's election.
WASHINGTON - The number of children schooled at home by their parents has doubled since 1990 to more than 500,000 but these students face many adjustments and challenges at college.
WASHINGTON - Sen. Trent Lott, who will be reelected Tuesday as Senate majority leader, calls for "order" not revolution.
WASHINGTON - A Richmond jury found a pattern of intentional race discrimination at Circuit City Stores Inc., one of the country's largest retailers of home electronics and appliances.
WASHINGTON - Sharpshooters, hunters and even timber wolves are among the options an increasing number of suburban Washington governments are considering to try to control a booming deer population.
